title: Black sesame cookies
subtitle: rich, crumbly butter cookies with tahini and toasted black sesame seeds
excerpt: Black sesame cookies are rich, crumbly butter cookies made with tahini and toasted black sesame seeds. The black sesame gives a deep, roasted, slightly nutty flavour and a striking dark-speckled appearance against the pale dough. The tahini in the dough adds softness and amplifies the sesame flavour. The cookies are short and tender, not chewy.
sourceNotes: Black sesame as a baking flavour documented in East Asian confectionery and baking traditions. Black sesame cookies in a European butter-cookie style became popular in British home baking alongside the wider interest in Japanese-inspired flavours from the 2010s onward.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze baked cookies in an airtight container for up to 2 months. Thaw at room temperature.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Keeps in an airtight tin at room temperature for up to 1 week.

content.text: Black sesame cookies are short, crumbly butter cookies made with tahini and toasted black sesame seeds. The black sesame gives a deep, roasted flavour and a striking speckled look. The dough is scooped and pressed flat rather than rolled; the texture is tender and slightly sandy rather than crisp.
Heat the oven to 175 degrees C (fan 155 degrees C / gas 4). Line two baking trays with baking paper.
Beat the softened butter, tahini, and icing sugar together until pale and creamy, about 2 minutes. Beat in the egg yolk.
Fold in the flour and black sesame seeds until just combined. The dough will be slightly sticky.
Scoop rounded teaspoons of dough and roll briefly into balls. Place on the prepared trays and press each ball flat with the palm of your hand to about 1 cm thick.
Bake for 12 to 14 minutes until the edges are just set and the undersides are very lightly golden. The cookies will still look soft but firm up as they cool.
Leave on the trays for 5 minutes before transferring to a rack to cool completely.

attrs.problem: Cookies spreading too thin and going flat
attrs.avoid: Avoid softened butter that is too warm or melted; very soft butter causes excessive spreading.
attrs.fix: Chill the shaped cookies on the tray for 20 minutes in the fridge before baking. Cold dough holds its shape better in the first few minutes of baking.

attrs.avoid: Avoid untoasted black sesame seeds; they have a much milder flavour than toasted.
attrs.fix: Toast the seeds in a dry frying pan for 2 minutes, tossing often, until fragrant. Use immediately after cooling.
